claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have one child - Alex, who's 8 years old and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Let me ask a few more questions to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Are you currently responsible for Alex's care - meaning you provide for their needs such as food, clothes, and general upkeep?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am responsible for Alex's care - I provide for all their needs like food, clothes, and everything they need.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Just one more important question:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or living with someone else, or do they live with you full-time?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, I am fostering Alex. They live with me full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that you're fostering Alex. This is an important detail. I need to ask one more question:

**Is the local council paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance costs?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure about that - I don't know if the council pays towards their accommodation or maintenance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - this can be a bit unclear sometimes. Let me ask it in a different way that might help:

**Do you receive any fostering allowance or payments from the local council for looking after Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I honestly don't know - I'm not sure whether I receive any payments from the council for fostering Alex or not.

## Assessment Summary

Based on the information you've provided, I'm unable to make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex at this time.

**Here's what I've found:**

You meet several key criteria:
- You live in the UK
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- Alex lives with you full-time
- You're responsible for Alex's care and provide for all their needs

**However**, there's a critical factor for foster carers: According to the rules, you can get Child Benefit if you foster a child, **as long as the local council is not paying anything towards their accommodation or maintenance**.

Since you're unsure whether you receive any fostering allowance or payments from the council, I cannot determine whether you're eligible or ineligible.

**What you need to do:**

To find out if you can claim Child Benefit, you'll need to check whether the local council pays you anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance. You could:
- Check your bank statements for any regular payments from the council
- Contact your fostering agency or social worker
- Speak directly with your local council

Once you have this information, you'll know whether you can apply for Child Benefit. If the council doesn't pay towards accommodation or maintenance, you should be eligible to claim.
